narrative.overview:
Comics solved silent sound by lettering it. Foley's cues are already onomatopoeia, so the page is a comic page: bright white stock, square panels drawn in a 3px ink line, one 14px gutter between every panel, and Bangers lettering with an ink outline and extrusion that names each cue as it plays. Colour is printed, not glowed: process yellow is the page's signal, seven flat family plates mark the cue families, and Ben-Day halftone dots are the only texture.

The page reads as panels laid on a grid, never as cards in a dashboard. Sections are unframed bands of paper; the framed things inside them are panels, and a panel is never put inside another framed section. Hand-lettered captions (Patrick Hand SC) sit in yellow boxes pinned to panel corners or as panel notes; speech balloons carry testimonials and toasts; code lives in night panels. Depth comes from line weight and halftone, not shadow.

The world is light only. There is no dark theme; night is a panel type, not a mode.
keyCharacteristics: Bright white paper, ink line art, square panel corners, one gutter.
Bangers SFX lettering, outlined and extruded in ink, shaped per letter by the cue's real envelope.
Process yellow as the single signal colour; seven family plates appear only where a family is named or playing.
Halftone dots as hover texture and as the flood when a cue plays.
Caption boxes and balloons in Patrick Hand SC carry the narrator's voice.
Night panels with a labelled header strip for every code sample.
Self-hosted fonts from `assets/fonts`; nothing loads from a font CDN.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Yellow is the only interface accent. Hover, selected, and primary states all resolve to yellow (or ink-on-paper inversion for segmented choices); a family plate never stands in for UI state.

rules.name: The Plate Discipline Rule
rules.body: A family colour appears only where its family is named or its cue is sounding. Canvases read plates through the page's `cssVar()` helper; no hex is hardcoded in script except as a fallback argument.

rules.name: The Flood Rule
rules.body: When a cue plays, its family plate floods the surface as halftone over a tint: dots at 70-75% plate over a 22-30% plate tint (stage 22% with 11px dots, tiles 30% with 9px dots). Floods are state, never resting decoration.

rules.name: The Lettering Rule
rules.body: SFX lettering is one construction: Bangers in a fill colour (`--fc`, default yellow) with an eight-direction 0.035em ink outline plus a two-step extrusion (0.05em/0.06em, 0.065em/0.08em), all in `text-shadow` so it renders on every engine. Because it is in em, it scales with the word. Lettered cue words split into per-letter spans sized by the cue's real envelope (`--v` = 0.56 + 0.44 x envelope) and tilted by its slope (`--tilt`, rotated from the letter's baseline).

rules.name: The Headings Are Lettered Rule
rules.body: H1, H2, and H3 are Bangers at weight 400 with tight line-height (0.9-1). Only the logo, the H1's second line, the stage word, pop-words, and the closing word get the full outline-and-extrusion treatment; section heads stay flat ink.

rules.name: The Narrator Rule
rules.body: Patrick Hand SC is for the narrator (captions, balloons, notes). It never sets a heading, a button, or a label above a heading.

rules.name: The One Gutter Rule
rules.body: Panel-to-panel spacing is `--gut` and nothing else. If two framed things touch, they are separated by the gutter or they share a 2px inner divider inside one panel (the mixing desk); never an ad-hoc gap.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: Panels are never nested inside framed sections. Sections are unframed bands; panels sit directly on paper.

rules.name: The Divisible Grid Rule
rules.body: Never `repeat(auto-fit, minmax())` for panels with uneven content. Choose a column count that divides the item count, reserve text zones, and bottom-anchor metadata with `margin-top: auto`.

rules.name: The Printed Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from line weight and halftone. No box-shadows, no blur, no glow; hard offset slabs (`0 2px 0 #000`) are banned. Extrusion belongs to lettering only.

rules.name: The Line Weight Rule
rules.body: 3px is the panel line; 2-2.5px is control chrome; 2px is an inner divider; 1.5px is a chip or value tag. Never mix a panel at control weight.

dos: Do separate every panel by `--gut` (14px, 10px compact) and frame it in the 3px ink `--line` with square corners.
Do letter cue words with the shared `.sfx` construction (em-based outline and extrusion) and per-letter `--v` and `--tilt` from the cue's envelope.
Do flood a surface with its family plate while its cue sounds: halftone at 70-75% over a 22-30% tint.
Do pin caption boxes into panel corners or panel feet, in Patrick Hand SC on yellow.
Do put every code sample in a night panel with a labelled 40px header strip.
Do read colours in canvases through `cssVar()`, with hex only as the fallback argument.
Do load fonts from `assets/fonts` and keep the page light.
Do honour reduced motion: the slam, burst, pop-word, marquee, and toasts collapse to instant.
donts: Don't nest a panel inside a framed section, or frame a section band.
Don't use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax())` for panels; pick column counts that divide the item count.
Don't add box-shadows, glows, or hard offset slabs; depth is line and halftone.
Don't put a caption box, kicker, or eyebrow label above a heading.
Don't use a family plate as UI state or decoration; state is yellow or ink inversion.
Don't invent new control chrome; reuse the button, segmented control, and knob.
Don't ship a dark theme or load fonts from a CDN.
